notes.text: The reciprocal entry supplies the exact Yerushalmi locus. Yonah, Chiyya and Shimon ben Lakish jointly cite Yudan Nesia on seven days of mourning.
The checked Yerushalmi has Yonah in Rabbi Abaye’s name in the discussion of terumah poured between vessels. Its digital section is 5:2:2. Preserve Heilprin’s received halakhah.
Yonah asks in Rav Hoshaya’s name about separately cooked fish and leeks mixed later.
Yonah in Rav Hamnuna’s name permits casual eating before Shabbat even after plucking for Shabbat.
Yonah transmits in Rabbi Chiyya bar Ba’s name the notice on the sages at the Valley of Rimmon.
Yonah in Rabbi Chiyya bar Vava’s name gives the alternative sequence of questions about selling a Torah scroll.
Yonah and Yose Gelila appear together transmitting in Rabbi Yasa bar Chanina’s name about study before the bier.
Yonah transmits in Bar Kappara’s name regarding the consecration days, the red heifer and the Yom Kippur goat.
The matched passage groups Yonah, Shmuel Kappadokaya and another sage in a debate on how much is required for neutralization. Its concise transition does not independently assign each opinion.
The parallel explicitly includes both Berekhiah and Yonah transmitting in the name of Resh Lakish in the name of Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi. Preserve the shorter received wording.
The earlier Zeaira discussion points to the Babylonian Zeira form and qualifies the scope of any identification. The internal target is the discussion, without deciding the name variants.
One of the two Bekhorot pairings explicitly calls Yonah a student of Zeaira. Retain Heilprin’s wording and preserve the alternative pairing in the adjacent Yonah entry.
The reciprocal notice and Yerushalmi document Acha bar Ulla receiving tithes from Yonah. This gives a comparison for the bare name without turning it into a status or relationship claim.
Inai approaches Yonah in the case of redemption on a coin. The bare roster receives no added role.
The Yerushalmi explicitly has Elazar bar Marom raise an objection before Yonah. Preserve the ben form in Heilprin’s heading and the bar form in the comparator.
The Yoma passage lists Ashyan and Yonah among transmitters in Yochanan’s name. The bare roster has no direction of transmission.
The associated Moed Katan passage gives Yonah going to Guryon. Preserve the bare name as printed.
